problem:
For the function $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, you're given the following data:

$$
f(e)=1,\,{f}^{′}(e)=\frac{1}{e},\,g(e)={e}^{2},\,{g}^{′}(e)=2e
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=e.$

feedback.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
f(-7)=2\sqrt{3},\,{f}^{′}(-7)=\sqrt{3},\,g(-7)=5\sqrt{3}\,{g}^{′}(-7)=-4\sqrt{3}
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=-7.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))=f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=-7,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=-7} & =f(-7){g}^{′}(-7)+g(-7){f}^{′}(-7) \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\cdot (-4\sqrt{3})+5\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{3} \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$
